articles.title: Non-destructive editing
articles.summary: Your original file is never written to. Every edit is a layer that can be turned off.
articles.body:
Nothing you do rewrites the file you started from. Each change is a [[layer]] sitting on top, and turning it off or deleting it returns the photo exactly as it was.

That is why you can come back a week later and still take one thing back without losing the rest.

articles.title: Layer
articles.summary: One change, stacked on the photo. It can be hidden, masked, faded or deleted at any time.
articles.body:
One change, stacked on the photo. Every layer works the same way: give it a [[mask]] and it applies only where you say, give it a [[blend_mode|blend mode]] and it combines with what is underneath instead of covering it.

Drop its [[opacity]] and you get less of whatever it does.

parameters.name: Adjust
parameters.what: The layer's own settings; the panel differs per kind.

parameters.name: Blend
parameters.what: Blend mode, opacity, channels and [[blend_if|Blend If]].

parameters.name: Mask
parameters.what: Where it applies. Empty means everywhere.

articles.title: Stack
articles.summary: Layers are applied from the bottom up. Order changes the result.
articles.body:
The photo sits at the bottom and never moves. Everything above it is applied in order, each [[layer]] seeing the result of everything beneath.

Move one up or down and the result changes: a [[curves|Curves]] under a [[black_white|Black & White]] is not the same picture as one above it.

articles.title: Adjustment layer
articles.summary: A layer that changes color or tone rather than adding pixels.
articles.body:
A layer that changes color or tone instead of adding pixels. [[curves|Curves]], [[exposure|Exposure]], [[hue_saturation|Hue & Saturation]] are all adjustment layers.

The + on the rail adds one; the capsule above it is the [[layer_stack|stack]]: scroll it to pick which layer the bar at the bottom is addressing.

articles.title: Group
articles.summary: Several layers folded into one, with their own opacity, blend mode and mask.
articles.body:
Everything inside runs in order first, then the group's own settings apply to the net result, so one [[opacity]] slider dials back the whole recipe at once, and one [[mask]] confines all of it.

By default a group is pass-through: the layers inside see the real photo beneath the group, exactly as if it were not there. Turning that off isolates them, so they see only each other.

parameters.name: Opacity
parameters.what: Fades everything inside, together.

parameters.name: Blend mode
parameters.what: How the group's net result meets what is under it.

parameters.name: Mask
parameters.what: Confines the whole group at once.

parameters.name: Pass-through
parameters.what: On: layers inside see through to the photo. Off: they see only the group.

parameters.name: Channels
parameters.what: Turning one off reverts that channel to the backdrop for everything inside.

articles.title: Project
articles.summary: A photo plus its layer stack, saved and reopenable.
articles.body:
A photo plus its [[layer_stack|stack]], saved together. Reopening one puts you back exactly where you stopped.

The original file is kept untouched alongside the edits; see [[non_destructive|nothing is overwritten]].

articles.title: Histogram
articles.summary: How much of the photo sits at each brightness, drawn as a graph.
articles.body:
How much of the photo sits at each brightness: shadows left, highlights right, height is how many pixels.

A spike against either wall means detail is being lost there. It describes; it does not judge: a night shot is supposed to lean left.

articles.title: Channel
articles.summary: The red, green and blue records that make up a color image.
articles.body:
A color photo is three grayscale records, red, green and blue, stacked on each other.

The selector appears wherever a tool can work on one at a time: [[curves|Curves]] and [[levels|Levels]] both take a channel, [[blend_if|Blend If]] can trigger on one, and [[channel_mixer|Channel Mixer]] builds each output channel from all three. On the [[blend_mode|blend]] panel the R / G / B toggles do something different again: they stop the layer writing to a channel at all.

parameters.name: RGB
parameters.what: All three at once, the usual case.

parameters.name: R / G / B
parameters.what: One record at a time. This is where color casts get fixed.

parameters.name: Blend toggles
parameters.what: Not a selector: an off channel means the layer never writes to it.

articles.title: LUT
articles.summary: A lookup table that maps every color to another one. The engine here needs none.
articles.body:
A lookup table maps every color to another one, once, for the whole picture. It is fast and it is fixed: you cannot ask it why.

The [[filters|filters]] here are built on tables. Everything else in the editor is real math on the pixels, which is what lets you tune it after the fact.

articles.title: Exposure
articles.body: Overall brightness, in stops, the way a camera means it. Offset shifts the blacks; Gamma bends the midtones.

parameters.name: Exposure
parameters.what: Overall brightness, in stops.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.what: Lifts or drops the blacks.

parameters.name: Gamma
parameters.what: Bends the midtones, leaving black and white where they are.

articles.title: Brightness & Contrast
articles.body: The blunt pair. Fast and obvious; [[curves]] or [[levels]] give you the same thing with control over where it lands.

parameters.name: Brightness
parameters.what: Everything up or down together.

parameters.name: Contrast
parameters.what: Pushes tones away from the middle, or toward it.

articles.title: Vignette
articles.body: Darkens or lightens the corners to hold the eye in the middle. Size, softness and roundness are yours.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.what: Darkens the corners, or lightens them.

parameters.name: Midpoint
parameters.what: How far in from the edge it starts.

articles.title: Grain
articles.body: Adds film grain. Size and roughness are separate, because 35mm and medium format do not look alike.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.what: How much grain.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.what: How large each grain is.

parameters.name: Roughness
parameters.what: How uneven the grain field is.

articles.title: Posterize
articles.body: Cuts the number of levels per [[channel]], so smooth gradients break into flat bands.

parameters.name: Levels
parameters.what: How many steps per channel. Fewer means broader, flatter bands.

articles.title: Image layer
articles.body: The photo itself, at the bottom of the [[layer_stack|stack]]. It cannot be deleted or reordered, and for a [[raw|RAW]] file it carries the [[develop]] settings.

articles.title: Mask
articles.summary: Where a layer applies, and how strongly. White applies, black does not.
articles.body:
Where a layer applies, and how strongly. White applies, black does not, gray applies partly.

A mask is built from [[mask_component|components]] (a [[gradient]], a [[brush]], a [[subject]]), which stack on each other.

articles.title: Mask component
articles.summary: One source of selection in a mask. Several stack, each adding, subtracting or intersecting.
articles.body:
One source of selection. Several stack in a list, each [[mask_mode|adding, subtracting or intersecting]] with what is beneath it.

So "the sky, but not the building" is two components, not one clever one.

articles.title: Add, subtract, intersect
articles.summary: How a component folds into the mask beneath it.
articles.body:
How a [[mask_component|component]] folds into the ones below. Add widens the selection, subtract cuts out of it, intersect keeps only the overlap.

The first component in a mask has nothing to combine with, so its mode is ignored.

articles.title: Brush mask
articles.summary: Paint the selection by hand.
articles.body:
Paint the selection by hand. Size, hardness and opacity are yours; painting with erase on takes it back.

An unpainted brush selects nothing: the layer stays hidden until you make the first stroke.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.what: How wide the stroke is.

parameters.name: Hardness
parameters.what: How soft its edge is.

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.what: Turns a non-round brush tip.

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.what: Round, square or triangular.

articles.title: Gradient mask
articles.summary: A linear or radial falloff, dragged across the frame.
articles.body:
A smooth fall from applied to not applied, dragged across the frame. Linear for a horizon, radial for a spot.

The classic use is a sky: drag from the top down and the [[layer]] fades out before it reaches the ground.

parameters.name: Start / End
parameters.what: Drag the two handles across the photo to set where the fall runs.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.what: How gradual the fall is.

parameters.name: Style
parameters.what: Linear for a horizon, radial for a spot.

articles.title: Luminosity mask
articles.summary: Select by brightness: shadows only, highlights only, or a band between.
articles.body:
Select by brightness rather than by place. Pick a band (shadows only, highlights only, something between) and the layer lands only there.

Fade softens the edge of the band, which is the difference between a natural result and a visible step.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.what: Which brightnesses are selected: shadows, highlights, or a band between.

parameters.name: Fade
parameters.what: Softens the band's edges. Without it the selection has a visible step.

articles.title: Subject mask
articles.summary: The main subject, found automatically. Needs a device that can run it.
articles.body:
Finds the main subject and selects it, no painting required. Runs on the device, and needs a recent one.

It is a starting point rather than a finish: add a [[brush]] component on top to fix what it missed.

parameters.name: Refine
parameters.what: Grows or shrinks the found edge.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.what: Softens it.

articles.title: Depth mask
articles.summary: Select by distance from the camera.
articles.body:
Selects by distance from the camera, using the depth the photo was captured with or an estimate made on the device.

Useful for pushing a background back without touching the person in front of it.

parameters.name: Near / Far
parameters.what: The distance band that gets selected.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.what: Softens the band's edges.

articles.title: Feather
articles.summary: How soft the edge of a mask is.
articles.body:
How soft the edge of a mask is. Zero is a cut; higher blurs the transition over more pixels.

Almost every mask wants a little. A hard edge is what makes an edit look pasted on.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.what: How soft the mask edge is. Zero is a cut.

articles.title: Density
articles.summary: How strongly a mask applies at full white.
articles.body:
How strongly a mask applies where it is fully white. Drop it and the whole mask gets gentler without redrawing anything.

Different from [[opacity]], which fades the layer itself.

parameters.name: Density
parameters.what: How strongly the mask applies where it is fully white.

articles.title: Invert
articles.summary: Swap what a mask selects for what it does not.
articles.body:
Swaps what a mask selects for what it does not. Selected the sky and wanted the ground: one tap.

Works on a single [[mask_component|component]] as well as on the whole mask.

articles.title: Mask overlay
articles.summary: The red tint that shows a mask while you are editing it.
articles.body:
The red tint shown while you edit a mask: it covers what the mask is hiding. It exists only on screen and is never in the export.

The name is borrowed from the red film used to cut masks by hand before any of this was digital.

articles.title: Blend mode
articles.summary: How a layer's result is combined with everything under it.
articles.body:
How a layer's result is combined with everything under it, rather than simply covering it. Multiply darkens, Screen lightens, Soft Light adds contrast around the midtones.

Normal is the plain answer: what the layer produced, at its [[opacity]].

parameters.name: Normal
parameters.what: The layer's result, at its opacity.

parameters.name: Multiply / Darken
parameters.what: Only darkens. White does nothing.

parameters.name: Screen / Lighten
parameters.what: Only lightens. Black does nothing.

parameters.name: Overlay / Soft Light
parameters.what: Adds contrast around the midtones.

articles.title: Opacity
articles.summary: How much of a layer reaches the result.
articles.body:
How much of the layer reaches the result. At 50% you get half the effect, whatever the effect is.

The fastest fix for an edit that is right in kind but too strong.

parameters.name: Opacity
parameters.what: How much of the layer reaches the result. At 50% you get half of whatever it does.

articles.title: Blend If
articles.summary: Restrict a layer to a range of tones in the layers beneath.
articles.body:
Restrict a layer to a range of tones in what is underneath. "Only where the photo is already dark", without drawing a [[mask]].

The handles split to make the cut-off gradual instead of a hard line.

parameters.name: This layer
parameters.what: Hides parts of this layer by their own brightness.

parameters.name: Underlying
parameters.what: Hides parts of it by the brightness of what is beneath.

parameters.name: Split handles
parameters.what: Drag a handle apart to make the cut-off gradual instead of hard.

articles.title: Clipping
articles.summary: Confine a layer to the one directly below it.
articles.body:
Confines a layer to the one directly below it, as if it were masked by that layer's shape.

Used to tune a single layer's result without letting the tuning spill onto the rest of the [[layer_stack|stack]].

articles.title: RAW
articles.summary: The sensor's own data, before a camera turned it into a picture.
articles.body:
The sensor's own reading, before a camera turned it into a picture. Bigger files, more room to move, highlights and white balance especially.

A phone's RAW is often partly processed already; a dedicated camera's usually is not.

articles.title: Develop
articles.summary: Turning RAW sensor data into an image: exposure, white balance, detail.
articles.body:
Turning [[raw|RAW]] sensor data into an image: exposure, white balance, contrast, detail. It runs before any [[layer]] does.

It is not a one-way step: the original file stays, so you can develop it differently later.

parameters.name: Exposure / Contrast
parameters.what: The starting point, before any layer.

parameters.name: White balance
parameters.what: Temperature and tint, with the sensor's full range to move in.

parameters.name: Detail
parameters.what: Sharpening and noise reduction, applied at demosaic time.

articles.title: Decoder version
articles.summary: Which generation of the system's RAW converter developed this file.
articles.body:
Which generation of the system's RAW converter produced the image. Newer generations demosaic and denoise differently.

Stamped into a [[project]] when the photo is imported, so nothing you have already edited changes underneath you.

articles.title: Crop
articles.summary: Change the frame. Reversible, like everything else.
articles.body:
Change the frame. Reversible like everything else: the pixels outside are kept, not thrown away.

Straightening lives here too.

parameters.name: Aspect
parameters.what: Free, or locked to a ratio.

parameters.name: Straighten
parameters.what: Rotates within the frame to level a horizon.

parameters.name: Flip / Rotate
parameters.what: Ninety degrees at a time, or mirrored.

articles.title: Export
articles.summary: Render the stack and save or share the result.
articles.body:
Renders the [[layer_stack|stack]] at full resolution and saves or shares the result. What you see on screen is a smaller [[proxy]]; the export is not.

Your [[project]] stays exactly as it was.

articles.title: Adjust
articles.summary: Light and color in one pass, without opening the full editor.
articles.body:
The quick route: exposure, contrast, warmth and saturation as plain sliders on one screen.

Everything here exists as a [[layer]] in the editor too; this is the same math with fewer decisions.

articles.title: Auto
articles.summary: One tap that reads the photo and sets the sliders for you.
articles.body:
It is a chip inside [[adjust|Adjust]], not a tool of its own: it moves the same sliders you can then move yourself, so nothing about it is a black box.

It reads the [[histogram]] and sets exposure and contrast from what it finds. Disagree with it and drag.

articles.title: Alchemy
articles.summary: Blend several looks on a pad and keep what comes out.
articles.body:
Drag a point around a pad whose corners are different styles; the result is a live mix of them. Roll the dice for a starting point you would not have chosen.

What you land on can be saved as a [[look]] and used like any other.

articles.title: Colorize
articles.summary: Adds color to a black and white photo.
articles.body:
Runs a model on the device; nothing is uploaded. Best on real monochrome originals; a photo that was color and got desaturated has less for it to work from.

The result lands as an ordinary [[layer]], so you can mask it or fade it.

articles.title: Portrait Blur
articles.summary: Throws the background out of focus, after the fact.
articles.body:
Finds the subject and blurs everything else, with the falloff following [[depth]] where the photo carries it.

Aperture sets how strong the blur is; the edge is where the work shows, so check hair against a bright background.

articles.title: Pipeline
articles.summary: A walk through your own edit, layer by layer.
articles.body:
Shows the photo rebuilt one [[layer]] at a time, from the original up to the result: what each layer contributed, in order.

The fastest way to understand a [[look]] you did not build yourself.
